paragraphs: Ashi. Huna bar Ashi; Chiyya, Chama, Chanin, Rav Chisda, Rav Yehudah, Yitzchak, Ulla (I did not find it), and Shimi, each bar Ashi. [Glosses: (a) Shabbat 138b: Rav Ashi bar Idi; new editions and Asheri, Sheshet; uncorrected. Rif: Shishi, left uncorrected according to the gloss. Eruvin 102, beginning of b, same subject: Shila, also reportedly left uncorrected. The checked Rosh, Rif and Eruvin cap passage read Shisha. (b) Beitzah 37, end of b: Ashi from Yochanan; uncorrected. Same subject, Merubbeh 69 and Yesh Bekhor 52b, new editions: Assi from Yochanan; perhaps Rav Assi, Yochanan’s student. Zevachim 11b: Ashi from Yochanan; uncorrected. (c) Niddah 63a: Yehudah bar Shila from Ashi should be Assi; uncorrected. (d) Shabbat 11a: Yehoshua bar Rav Idi visits Rav Ashi—I think Assi, as Ta'anit’s parallel. (e) Zevachim 55b: Yaakov bar Acha from Ashi should be Assi; uncorrected. (f) Beitzah 6a: Ravina before Rav Assi; Rif and Asheri: Ashi; uncorrected. (g) Beitzah 6a, Gittin 59a: Mordekhai, Ashi’s student—Rashi cites Sotah 46b on escorting a teacher who is not one’s principal teacher for a parasang: Mordekhai escorted Ashi. Difficult: Berakhot 31a and Sotah have Rav Shimi bar Ashi; likewise Ein Yaakov and new Berakhot editions. But the new Sotah editions have Ashi. The gloss concludes that one new-edition reading is erroneous. The checked Sotah has Rav Ashi, while the checked Berakhot and Glick Ein Yaakov have Rav Shimi bar Ashi.]
